metadata.name: [GCP Cloud SQL MySQL OTel] Instance metrics not reporting
metadata.description: Alerts when a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance that reported metrics in the last 2 hours has sent no Cloud SQL metric for at least 20 minutes, about four times the normal 3-5 minute delivery delay. The other rules can't evaluate an instance that has no data, so this rule is what catches a stopped collector, failing Cloud Monitoring API access or a deleted instance. The alert recovers when data resumes, or after 2 hours of silence, once the instance leaves the window. One missing data point never triggers it.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.cloudsql_mysql.otel-*
| WHERE resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "cloudsql_database"
// Newest sample of any Cloud SQL metric per instance, plus the MySQL marker
| STATS last_sample = MAX(`@timestamp`),
        marker = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/mysql/queries`))
  BY database_id

breach.segment:
WHERE marker > 0
| EVAL minutes_since_last_sample = DATE_DIFF("minute", last_sample, NOW())
// Threshold: 20 minutes, about four times the normal 3-5 minute Cloud Monitoring delivery delay.
// Raise it if the receiver collection_interval is longer than 5 minutes.
| WHERE minutes_since_last_sample >= 20
| SORT minutes_since_last_sample DESC, database_id ASC
| LIMIT 100
| KEEP database_id, last_sample, minutes_since_last_sample

data.content:
## Cloud SQL MySQL instance metrics not reporting

No Cloud SQL metric has arrived for this instance for `minutes_since_last_sample` minutes. While data is missing, every other rule is blind for this instance. Their alerts recover because no data means no breach.

### Triage
1. Check whether **all** instances are affected (look at the *List of instances* in **[GCP OTel] Cloud SQL MySQL Overview**) or only this one.
2. All or many instances: check the OpenTelemetry collector running the `googlecloudmonitoring` receiver. Look at its health, its logs for Cloud Monitoring API errors (permissions, quota, expired credentials) and its exporter errors to Elasticsearch.
3. One instance: check whether the instance was deleted, renamed or moved to another project, and whether the receiver's project list or metric filters changed.
4. Check that the instance still exists and is publishing metrics in Cloud Monitoring (Metrics Explorer, `cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/up`).

### Notes
- An alert recovers after 2 hours of silence, even if data never resumes, because the instance drops out of the lookback window. Treat that recovery with care.
- Raise the 20-minute threshold if the receiver's `collection_interval` is longer than 5 minutes.
